business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Absorbable Polyglycolic Acid Braided Sutures

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France — single national corporate registry system (Registre National des Entreprises, RNE); no sub-state or provincial incorporation registry division
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code lineage; French Commercial Code, Civil Code, Monetary and Financial Code, Code of Public Health)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between France and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 30 May 1984; amended by Protocol of 26 Nov 2013; in force 1 Jan 2015)
Convention between France and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 1967; as amended by Protocols of 1970, 1984, 2006 and 2009)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée), L.210-1 and L.210-2 (formation formalities), R.223-1 and R.210-1 (regulatory implementation), supplemented by Law PACTE n° 2019-486 and Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) for medical-device manufacturing scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) — one-stop electronic filing via the INPI Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) together with the company creation declaration (formerly formulaire M0 / déclaration de création d'entreprise) lodged with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for the SARL (may be freely set at €1 in the Statuts). Under Article L.223-7 of the Commercial Code, cash contributions must be paid up to at least 20% upon subscription, with the balance payable within five years; in-kind contributions must be fully paid at incorporation. All cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and may be released only upon presentation of the Kbis extract after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding shareholders of [Company Name] Société à Responsabilité Limitée, convened on [Date], adopt the Statuts as drafted and approve the subscription of share capital in the amount of EUR [X], paid up in cash and in kind in accordance with Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code; that the registered office be fixed at [Address]; that [Manager Name] be appointed Gérant for an indefinite term with full powers of management and representation; and that the Gérant be authorized to complete all filings with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the INPI Guichet Unique, to publish the incorporation notice, and to take all steps necessary to obtain the Kbis extract and commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders; notary public (Notaire) required when real-property or certain in-kind contributions are made.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts covering legal form, corporate purpose (manufacture and assembly of absorbable surgical sutures and surgical needles), share capital, registered-office rules, and Gérant powers. Every founder must sign physically or with an eIDAS-qualified electronic signature. If any in-kind contribution has a value exceeding €30,000 or represents more than half of the share capital, the partners must jointly petition the President of the Tribunal de Commerce to appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) whose valuation report must be attached before execution.
required_dossiers: Valid identity document of each founding shareholder
Valuation report of the commissaire aux apports (if in-kind contributions apply)
Notarized power of attorney for any shareholder represented on signing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the contested clauses and re-execute the Statuts; if a notary refuses due to unlawful provisions, revise the corporate purpose or management clauses before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit share capital in a blocked account and obtain the depository certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (banque) or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the company in formation, transfer the subscribed cash contributions, and collect the 'certificat du dépositaire des fonds'. The funds remain frozen until the company is registered; release is authorized solely upon presentation of the Kbis extract to the financial institution.
required_dossiers: Project Statuts of the company in formation
Bank account RIB/IBAN and AML/KYC information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depository certificate is refused, complete the capital payment, correct AML documentation, or obtain a corrected attestation from an alternative bank before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation dossier with the INPI Guichet Unique and register with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (single electronic window) in coordination with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic declaration of company creation on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, upload the signed Statuts and all supporting attachments, and pay the official registration fee online. The Greffe verifies statutory legality, checks beneficial-owner declarations, registers the company in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, and issues the official Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Justificatif de jouissance des locaux (proof of lawful occupancy of the registered office)
Certificat de dépôt des fonds (blocked-capital depository certificate)
Acte de nomination du Gérant and déclaration de non-condamnation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond in writing to the Greffe's observations or refusal within the prescribed deadline, correct the defective items, and re-file; a contested refusal may be appealed to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce by direct application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Kbis extract and complete post-registration operational set-up
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; automatic notifications to INSEE (SIREN/SIRET), URSSAF, DGFiP and the competent welfare institutions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the Kbis extract evidencing legal existence; present it to the depository bank to release the blocked capital; register for VAT and employer obligations with the tax and social authorities; and, as a medical-device manufacturer, create the EUDAMED entity registration of the French legal manufacturer before commercial production.
required_dossiers: RIB and opening balance sheet information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any factual error in the RCS entry by filing an 'inscription rectificative' with the Greffe; if the SIREN/SIRET identifiers are missing, request immediate INSEE reconciliation and close any URSSAF declaration gap.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) for industrial and labor authorization, in coordination with the Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM) for medical-device manufacturing compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CE Marking of the Medical Device under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) — Class IIa/III absorbable sutures — plus ANSM manufacturer declaration (Code de la santé publique, Articles L.5211-1 and L.5212-5) and EUDAMED registration of the legal manufacturer.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) under the French Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement, ICPE regime).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Enregistrement (Registration) — Installations Classées Rubrique 2560 (work on metals) and Rubrique 2450 (surface treatment via electrolysis or chemical baths, if installed); simplified Environmental Impact Assessment dossier required with quantified emission inventory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits: pH 5.5–8.5, total suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L; VOC emissions ≤ 110 mg C/m³ with abatement efficiency ≥ 98% under Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive) and the relevant ministerial orders; zero chromium(VI) in treated effluents; all hazardous production waste covered by bordereaux de suivi des déchets and treated by authorized facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and favourable opinion of the Commission de sécurité (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours); structural load inspection certified by an approved technical control bureau (bureau de contrôle); workplace clearance covering ISO 14644 cleanroom classification, electrical installation certification, emergency evacuation planning, pressure-equipment verification, and prior operational declaration to DREETS for occupational health and safety compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — French Public Finance Directorate, acting through the Divisional Tax Offices for Enterprises (SIE) and the non-resident tax services; online portal: www.impots.gouv.fr. Customs export and import formalities are separately administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned French SARL is first registered with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Guichet Unique formalities portal operated by INPI, obtaining a SIREN number and SIRET establishment number. The DGFiP then allocates the French corporate income tax (IS) account and the French VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) to the registered entity. A foreign entity with a permanent establishment or direct taxable activity in France must file a tax registration application with the competent SIE or the DGFiP non-resident service, provide corporate authorisation, proof of foreign registration, director identification and a fiscal representative appointment where the entity is not established in the EU. The issued VAT number is also used as the French tax identification number for dealings with customs (EORI), suppliers and customers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is by default subject to entity-level corporation tax (IS). Eligible SARLs may elect, under Article 239 bis AA of the French General Tax Code, to be taxed as a partnership (régime des sociétés de personnes) for a limited period, causing profits to be taxed at the shareholder level as passthrough income; a similar family-company option exists under Article 239 bis AB. No check-the-box election is available in France; the IS/IR election is the functional equivalent for entity classification. For VAT, affiliated persons may elect to form a single taxable person (assujetti unique / VAT group) under Article 256 C III of the CGI. France does not allow election around hybrid mismatch rules; EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) provisions are mandatorily applied.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: An entity established in France must register for VAT when it commences regular economic activity, regardless of turnover, unless it qualifies for the small-business exemption known as 'franchise en base de TVA' (annual turnover not exceeding EUR 85,000 for sales of goods and EUR 34,400 for services; higher adjusted thresholds apply in certain cases). A manufacturing SARL making surgical sutures will generally be required to be VAT-registered because it engages in continuous supplies and must recover input VAT; the franchise exemption is not available where the business applies export zero-rating and needs input VAT recovery. For non-resident suppliers of intra-EU distance sales to France, the annual distance-selling threshold is EUR 10,000 for all cross-border distance sales within the EU; exceeding this threshold triggers French VAT registration unless the OSS/IOSS regime is used.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is progressively mandating electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting. From 1 September 2026, all VAT-taxable businesses must be able to receive e-invoices, and large businesses must issue e-invoices through either the public Chorus Pro portal or a certified Partner Dematerialisation Platform (PDP). From 1 September 2027, e-invoicing becomes mandatory for smaller entities, including micro-enterprises, and e-reporting of cross-border transaction data must be delivered electronically to the DGFiP. The regime operates through structured PDF and API/AS4 exchanges to the PDP; there is currently no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping/crypto-stamping system at DGFiP level, although the PDP must transmit invoice data in a standardised format. Invoicing to public-sector bodies already requires structured e-invoices through Chorus Pro.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the European Union qualify for the French 0% VAT rate (exonération de TVA avec droit à déduction) under Article 262-I of the French General Tax Code (CGI) when the seller proves that the goods were physically transported outside the EU in accordance with customs formalities, a valid export declaration exists, and transport and commercial documentation demonstrate delivery to the foreign destination. Directly connected logistics services and certain offshore services supplied to a non-EU recipient may also be zero-rated under Articles 262-II, 263 and 259 CGI where the place of supply is outside France and the benefit is genuinely located abroad. The exporter must retain contemporaneous, consistent and credible evidence; without this proof, the transaction is reclassified as a taxable domestic supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration Unique d'Exportation / DAU) accepted by the DGDDI
Bill of Lading, airway bill, CMR or equivalent transport document evidencing movement from France to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 evidence of receipt of export proceeds
Packing list, certificate of origin and, where relevant, exit summary declaration validation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP conducts strict export-audit scrutiny of zero-rate claims, especially for goods with high unit value such as surgical consumables. If the export evidence is incomplete, contradictory or fabricated, VAT is reassessed at 20% on the invoice amount, with monthly late-payment interest (intérêt de retard), and penalties of 40% are applied for intentional fault (mauvaise foi) or up to 80% for fraudulent behaviour; restitution and clawback of previously refunded input VAT and export VAT refunds are ordered. Criminal prosecution for tax fraud may result in fines of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years. Customs authorities may also impose penalties for false customs declarations or unlawful use of the export regime. The ordinary audit limitation period is six years, extended to ten years (or longer) where fraud, fictitious invoices or concealment are established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Full name of the Central Bank or Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Analysis of capital vs current account convertibility and profit remittance hurdles
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline and mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating and legal constraints regarding offshore digital EMIs
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Whether directors must appear physically or if remote opening is permitted

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle required to satisfy compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 month after General Meeting approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to 1,500 EUR plus potential administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Liasse Fiscale including Form 1203)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 0.5% of tax due per month of delay, maximum 25% of tax due
Penalty of 0.5% of unreported turnover per month of delay
Late filing penalties and interest charges

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Turnover exceeding 800,000 EUR or total assets exceeding 400,000 EUR

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual UBO register update with tax authorities upon ownership changes or as requested

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax, generally applicable to French companies and French permanent establishments. A reduced 15% rate may apply to qualifying small and medium-sized companies on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to applicable turnover, capital ownership and paid-up-capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: France generally provides no broad corporate tax holiday. Relevant incentives may include the 15% SME rate on qualifying profit, the research tax credit generally equal to 30% of eligible research expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, the innovation tax credit for qualifying SMEs, accelerated or exceptional depreciation regimes where legislated, and regional or sector-specific aid subject to European Union State-aid limits. Tax credits and incentives require contemporaneous substantiation and may be subject to recapture.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward. Utilisation is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Tax losses may generally be carried back only to the immediately preceding financial year, subject to statutory limits and an election.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, together with the applicable results schedules Form 2050-SD through Form 2059-G-SD, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal impots.gouv.fr using EDI-TDFC or EFI where available.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly or periodic instalments during the financial year, with the final balance payment after filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year. For a financial year ending on another date, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The final corporate income tax balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, subject to the applicable electronic payment calendar. Four instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, unless an exception applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, financial year dates, tax regime, tax-consolidation status, and relevant filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not file this return merely because it owns shares in the SARL. The French SARL files as a French resident entity. A non-resident enterprise files only for a French permanent establishment, taxable French business activity, or other applicable French filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD, taxable profit or loss and corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss, taxable result after tax adjustments, corporate income tax, tax credits, instalments, withholding credits and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only profits attributable to the French entity or French permanent establishment under French domestic law and applicable treaty principles. Exclude foreign-source profits that are not attributable to France, subject to anti-abuse, permanent-establishment and tax-consolidation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between accounting result and taxable result, including permanent and temporary add-backs, non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation differences, exempt income and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose deductions and add-backs relating to transactions with non-resident related parties, including interest limitation, withholding tax, non-deductible expenses and treaty-exempt income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward, losses utilised in the current year, remaining losses and any loss carryback claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only losses legally attributable to the French taxpayer or French permanent establishment. A foreign group's losses cannot be imported into the SARL unless a specific French tax-consolidation or statutory mechanism applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation and computation of taxable profit, including tax-group adjustments where relevant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a standalone SARL, report the entity's French taxable result. For a French tax group, report the required entity-level and group-level amounts under the tax-integration rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets, securities and other capital items, including short-term and long-term classification where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French domestic sourcing rules and the relevant double tax agreement to disposals involving non-residents. Maintain evidence of acquisition cost, ownership period, beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information on related entities, shareholdings, controlled transactions and relevant group relationships.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify non-resident parent companies, subsidiaries, sister companies and controlled transactions, including procurement, contract manufacturing, royalties, loans, guarantees, management fees and cost allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claimed tax credits, including research, innovation and other applicable credits, with the required expenditure and eligibility details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder cannot claim the SARL's credits. The French SARL must retain evidence that the qualifying expenditure was incurred by the French taxpayer and satisfies French and European Union conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary information concerning controlled transactions, transfer-pricing methods, related parties and material transaction categories where the statutory filing threshold is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report controlled transactions with non-resident related parties and permanent establishments. The form does not replace full transfer-pricing documentation where the full documentation threshold applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% where the taxpayer fails to file after formal notice and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent activity or abusive conduct. Late payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Understatements may trigger a 10% surcharge for ordinary negligence, 40% for deliberate failure or failure after formal notice, and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law. Additional penalties may apply for inaccurate transfer-pricing declarations, missing documentation, prohibited tax arrangements, late payment of instalments and failure to use mandatory electronic filing or payment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder are generally subject to a 25% withholding tax under French domestic law, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. The French parent-subsidiary regime may reduce withholding to 0% for a qualifying EU or European Economic Area corporate parent meeting the minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions. Domestic withholding may also be reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's competent foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements where relevant, confirm the recipient's legal form and treaty eligibility, and retain ownership and holding-period evidence. The French payer should apply the reduced rate only where the treaty or domestic exemption conditions are satisfied and should obtain any required French administrative form or certificate. If relief cannot be applied at source, the payer should withhold at the domestic rate and the recipient may seek a refund from the French tax administration using the applicable treaty refund procedure. Anti-conduit, beneficial-ownership and anti-abuse rules must be reviewed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to non-residents may be subject to French withholding generally at 25% under domestic rules, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty reductions. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to 0%, 5%, 8%, 10% or 15%, depending on the treaty and category of payment. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions apply, including payments to entities in non-cooperative jurisdictions or payments recharacterised as distributions or subject to special anti-abuse rules. Treaty interest rates commonly range from 0% to 15%. Payments must be classified by substance; software, know-how, technical services, management services and lease payments may have different French sourcing and withholding treatment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full French transfer-pricing documentation is generally mandatory where the French enterprise or relevant French tax group meets the statutory EUR 150 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, or where it is owned by, owns, or belongs to a group containing an enterprise meeting the threshold, subject to the applicable statutory rules. A country-by-country report generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million. A simplified annual transfer-pricing declaration may apply from lower thresholds, including where annual turnover or gross assets reach EUR 50 million or the relevant controlled-transaction criteria are met. Materiality and transaction-category thresholds must be checked for the filing year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to certain offshore economic-substance regimes. Substance is enforced through transfer-pricing arm's-length rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, the abuse-of-law doctrine, the principal-purpose test, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation, anti-hybrid rules, withholding-tax anti-abuse provisions and general anti-avoidance principles. A French SARL manufacturing surgical consumables should maintain genuine French premises, equipment, personnel, production records, quality-control capacity, inventory and decision-making appropriate to its functions and risks. Intercompany royalties, management charges, financing, guarantees and procurement arrangements must correspond to actual services or rights and be priced at arm's length.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating purchases, maintaining parallel accounts, falsely deducting personal or shareholder expenditure, omitting taxable income, or manipulating inventory and production costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest and tax surcharges; tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, increased in aggravated cases to up to seven years and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions and judicial findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur criminal liability where they personally participate in the conduct. A court may impose management disqualification and confiscation. Under Article L267 of the French Tax Procedures Code, a director may be declared personally and jointly liable for tax debt where fraudulent manoeuvres or serious and repeated non-compliance made collection impossible. There is no automatic travel ban, but judicial control, passport restrictions or other measures may arise in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and undocumented related-party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, interest, guarantees or procurement prices; shifting French manufacturing profit offshore; failing to maintain required master-file or local-file documentation; or submitting materially inaccurate transfer-pricing information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary tax adjustment, withholding-tax assessment, interest and surcharges. Failure to produce required transfer-pricing documentation may attract a penalty generally calculated by reference to the amount of the reassessment, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. Inaccurate or incomplete declarations may generate separate fixed or percentage-based penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for deliberate misrepresentation, participation in fraud or obstruction of a tax audit. Ordinary economic disagreement does not automatically create personal liability, but repeated unsupported related-party charges materially increase reassessment and management-liability risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal dividend, hidden distribution and capital-maintenance breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without approved accounts or distributable reserves, paying disguised dividends through shareholder loans or personal expenses, or repatriating cash while concealing taxable distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate, recipient and withholding-tax reassessment; possible repayment of unlawful distributions; civil liability for management; and, depending on the conduct, criminal penalties for misuse of corporate assets, presentation of inaccurate accounts or tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be required to restore improperly distributed amounts and compensate the company or creditors. Criminal exposure may arise for misuse of company assets or false accounts. A separate automatic piercing of the corporate veil does not apply merely because the company is insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating French sales, claiming fictitious input VAT, misclassifying medical products, using false origin or tariff information, undervaluing imports, or routing goods through related entities to evade import VAT or customs duty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT and customs reassessment, interest, surcharges, seizure, administrative fines and possible criminal prosecution. Fraudulent VAT conduct may be prosecuted under the general tax-fraud framework, with aggravated sanctions where organised or deliberate concealment is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be liable for deliberate participation, customs offences or serious repeated compliance failures. Customs authorities may pursue the debtor, declarant, importer of record and responsible individuals according to the relevant customs and criminal provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, using opaque intermediaries, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions or adverse-media indicators, structuring payments to avoid controls, or failing to report suspicious activity where a regulated obligation applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative, regulatory and criminal consequences may include account restrictions, confiscation, fines, professional sanctions and prosecution. Money laundering may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 375,000, with aggravated cases carrying higher penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted for intentional laundering, aiding and abetting, concealment or facilitating transactions. Courts may impose confiscation and management prohibitions. A travel ban is not automatic and depends on judicial measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sanctions, export-control and medical-device regulatory breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exporting surgical sutures or needles to prohibited destinations or persons, bypassing EU sanctions, using false end-user documents, or placing non-compliant medical devices on the French or EU market without required conformity, traceability or quality-system controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative enforcement, product withdrawal, recall, customs seizure, licence restrictions, substantial fines and criminal prosecution may apply under EU sanctions, French customs law and medical-device legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal criminal exposure for knowing or negligent participation, particularly where false declarations, concealment or serious safety risks are involved. Civil claims may include product liability, customer damages and creditor claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominee shareholders, fictitious directors, circular invoicing, unsubstantiated management companies or offshore entities to conceal the ultimate beneficial owner, divert profits or avoid French tax and regulatory controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, abuse-of-law penalties, beneficial-owner filing sanctions, AML enforcement, confiscation and possible prosecution for fraud, money laundering or misuse of corporate assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable where they knowingly implement the concealment structure or frustrate tax collection. The corporate veil is not automatically pierced, but fraudulent manoeuvres and commingling of assets materially increase personal civil and criminal exposure.
